newsitem.title: FRANCE: France withholds support from U.S. raid on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: France withholds support from U.S. raid on Iraq.

text.p: France withheld support on Tuesday for a U.S. cruise missile attack on Iraq, while urging Baghdad to withdraw its forces from Kurdish areas of northern Iraq.
A Foreign Ministry statement said France had been "informed in advance of the operation conducted this morning by the United States" but made no comment on the merits of the raid.

French officials said President Bill Clinton telephoned President Jacques Chirac on Monday night to inform him of the impending action. Chirac made clear he understood Clinton's motives, in the midst of the U.S. presidential election campaign, but differed on the appropriateness of military action, they said.
Paris fought alongside the United States in the Gulf War to drive Iraq out of Kuwait in 1991 and is one of the allies enforcing no-fly zones in southern and northern Iraq.

"France expresses its concern at the development of the situation in Iraq," the Foreign Ministry statement said. "In a message sent last night by (Foreign Minister) Herve de Charette to Iraqi Vice-Prime Minister Tareq Aziz, France stressed the need to continue withdrawing effectively the forces involved on the ground, as the Iraqi authroities had announced on Sunday."

De Charette emphasized the international community's concern for the safety of the civilian population and said only a dialogue between Baghdad and the Kurdish factions could lead to the restoration of stability through a political settlement.
